Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Healthcare Services, Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Healthcare Services' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mark Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Laura Bennett, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Harris, Chief Operating Officer; and Karen Patel, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, with emphasis on our same-facility volume and revenue growth outlook, net patient revenue performance, revenue per admission dynamics, the effects of seasonality and external influences, same-facility admissions and patient day trends, and the drivers of our operating margins.

Let me begin with our outlook for same-facility volume and revenue growth heading into the fourth quarter ending December 31, 2024, and full fiscal year 2025. Our same-facility metrics exclude the effects of our recent divestiture of three underperforming rural facilities in the Midwest and the acquisition of two ambulatory surgery centers in the Southeast, which we will address in our M&A update later. We are seeing strong underlying demand fueled by an aging population—Medicare patients now make up 52% of our inpatient mix, up from 49% last year—and lingering elective procedure volumes following COVID disruptions. That said, we are moderating our expectations due to ongoing reimbursement pressures from CMS's FY2025 IPPS update, which provides just a 2.9% lump-sum increase after productivity adjustments and wage index reductions. Our payer mix is steady at 45% commercial, 52% government, and 3% self-pay/other, though Medicare Advantage denials, averaging 12% network-wide, are posing challenges.

For Q4 2024 same-facility guidance, we anticipate admissions growth of 3.0% to 3.5% year-over-year, with average daily census expanding to 1,850-1,900 beds, a 2% rise in occupied bed days. Outpatient volumes, our top-margin growth area, are projected to accelerate to 6.5%-7.0%, supported by a 10% increase in procedures at our 45 freestanding ASCs and hospital outpatient departments. ED visits should be flat to up 1.5%, as seasonal flu and RSV ease from Q3 highs but face offsets from lower-acuity non-urgent cases.

By service line, inpatient acute care should see 2.5% admissions growth, with case mix index stable at 1.85, bolstered by high-acuity orthopedics and neurology cases. Surgical volumes will benefit from OR utilization climbing to 68%-70% from 65% in Q3, driven by 12% growth in total joint replacements and spinal fusions, where our Centers of Excellence program is gaining share from independent providers. Observation and outpatient services are expected up 8%, including a 15% jump in cardiology cath lab procedures following our Medtronic partnership for TAVR expansions.

We guide Q4 revenue growth at 4.5%-5.0% same-facility, translating to net revenue per admission of $14,200-$14,500, a 1.5% sequential increase. This factors in 2.5%-3.0% commercial pricing gains from Blue Cross renegotiations, offset by a 1% hit from Medicaid redeterminations in expansion states. Total same-facility net patient revenue is forecasted at $2.45-$2.50 billion.

Extending to full-year 2025 same-facility guidance, we expect volume growth of 3.5%-4.0% and revenue growth of 5.0%-5.5%. Key tailwinds include our enterprise-wide Epic MyChart rollout, now active in 85% of facilities, boosting virtual visits by 20% and shifting low-acuity care to telehealth to free inpatient capacity. We're also deploying AI-powered revenue cycle tools from Change Healthcare, aiming for 150 basis points better cash collections and denial rates below 10%.

Regionally, Sunbelt areas—Florida, Texas, and Arizona, 60% of our footprint—are leading with 5%-6% volume growth from population shifts and stronger payer mixes at 50% commercial. Florida sites, for example, posted 8% ortho growth amid capacity limits at competitors like HCA in Tampa and Miami. Northeast facilities in New York and Pennsylvania face 1%-2% volume softness from 28% Medicaid penetration and union labor hikes, but value-based contracts with UnitedHealth's Optum provide shared savings relief.

Strategically, our Procedure-First approach emphasizes high-acuity, site-neutral expansion, including Humana partnerships for MSK ortho bundles yielding 15% EBITDA margins in pilots. Elective backlogs are 85% cleared, led by 18% YoY growth in spinal and bariatric procedures. Against 14% RN turnover, we've committed $150 million to workforce efforts, cutting travel nurses 40% and enhancing retention via Daisy Award programs.

Risks include government shutdown delays to Medicare payments and self-pay bad debt at 3.2%. Supply inflation is contained at 2.5% via Vizient GPO despite GLP-1 shortages affecting bariatrics. Overall, this guidance showcases disciplined execution for mid-single-digit growth with operational leverage.

Moving to net patient revenue, which reached $2.48 billion in Q3, up 8.7% year-over-year and 4.2% quarter-over-quarter. This extends our streak of 11 straight quarters of YoY gains, highlighting the resilience of our acute care platform in a post-pandemic recovery.

Adjusted admissions climbed 5.2% YoY to 142,000, powered by 7.1% elective procedure growth—orthopedics, TAVR, PCI, and general surgeries now at 105% of pre-COVID levels across our 45-hospital network. Outpatient volumes rose 9.8% YoY via ASCs and HOPDs, with equivalent patient days up 6.4% to 1.85 million and ALOS steady at 4.7 days due to clinical efficiencies.

Net revenue per admission rose 3.4% YoY to $14,250, from commercial escalators and CMI uptick to 1.82 from 1.78, driven by 12% YoY growth in cardiovascular MS-DRGs via Medtronic structural heart collaborations.

Commercial payers hit 48% of revenue, up 150 bps YoY from Blue Cross contracts. Medicare at 38% benefited from top-quartile value-based purchasing scores. Medicaid fell to 11% with $185 million charity care (6.9% gross revenue). Denials dropped to 4.2% from 5.1% via Epic MyChart and Change Healthcare AI, adding $22 million in collections.

QoQ growth from $2.38 billion stemmed from respiratory seasonal lifts (admissions +3.8%) and behavioral health ramp to 1,200 beds post-Pinnacle acquisition. EPDs +2.9% QoQ, outpatient mix to 62%.

Sunbelt markets (55% beds) grew 11.2% YoY revenue, Florida at $685 million up 13% via Optum MSK JVs. Midwest/Northeast up 4.1% via tele-ICU with Philips cutting ALOS 0.3 days.

This validates our high-growth, high-acuity strategy, with ASCs at 18% EBITDA vs. 12% inpatient. Tech like Cerner and Palantir uplifts revenue 2-3% per site. Q4 net patient revenue eyed at 7-9% YoY with 340B optimizations adding $15 million.

Next, revenue per admission trends, which hit $15,450 in Q3, up 5.2% YoY from $14,680 and 1.8% sequentially—stronger than HCA's 4.1% and Tenet's 3.8%. Same-facility RPA up 5.7% YoY, excluding divestitures and acquisitions.

Drivers: CMI to 1.92 (+2.3% YoY) from 12% cardiology/neurosurgery surge, TAVR/craniotomies at flagship Florida/Texas Level I centers (CMI 2.05 vs. AHA 1.75 avg).

Commercial RPA +6.8% YoY to $22,100 via 5.5% UnitedHealthcare/Anthem hikes, leveraging labor shortages (15% nurse vacancies). Epic Revenue Cycle cut denials 18%, realization to 92%.

Service lines: ortho +7% admissions (14% mix, RPA $28,500), oncology CAR-T/proton at $35,200. Behavioral/general medicine -3% via outpatient shift. LOS 4.6 days, geometric mean -2%.

Payer mix 45% commercial, 35% Medicare (+4.1% RPA to $13,800 on IPPS 2.7% and outliers $45M), 15% Medicaid ($9,200 offset by supplements). MA at 22%.

Southeast (45% beds) +6.5% RPA (Florida commercial/trauma, FEMA $120M post-hurricanes). Midwest +4.2% (Eli Lilly precision medicine). California +3.8% via tele-stroke.

Investing $250M in CDI/NLP tools for 150 bps CMI gain, 30% bundled payments. FY24 RPA 4.5-5.5%.

On seasonality and external factors, Q3 saw amplified respiratory pressures akin to peak flu/RSV, boosting adjusted admissions 14% YoY to 128,000 and net patient revenue 17% to $2.8 billion. Inpatient revenue +19% (62% mix), EPDs +16% to 1.2M, ADC record 4,850 beds.

ED volumes +22% QoQ, FLI 28% of visits, ED conversion to 34%. CMI +2.1% to 1.85 (pneumonia/sepsis), ALOS 4.6 days via Epic discharge tools.

Northeast (Richmond/Charlotte) +21% admissions, peds RSV +35% filling 85% of 250 PICU beds (42% vax rates). Sunbelt +9%, offset by ortho/cardio post-hurricanes.

H1N1 early/aggressive + RSV/COVID (8% FLI), respiratory tests +41% to 150K ($45M at $300/test). MA denials +3% to 12%.

Costs: labor +11% QoQ to $850M (contract 8%), ShiftMed AI scheduling. Supplies +16%, Vizient flu vax $18/dose.

FluSense AI (Google Cloud/Biobot) forecasts spikes, flex 15% capacity (88% occupancy vs. 75% industry). Teladoc bundles cut readmissions 22%.

FY25 flu eyed earlier (El Niño), budgeted 12-15% Q4 volume, $150M bed adds, ASC shift (25% revenue).

Incremental EBITDA $420M from peaks, tech tames volatility.

Turning to same-facility admissions and patient days: Q3 admissions +5.2% YoY, +2.1% QoQ—7th straight positive, accelerating from Q1's 4.1%, beating HCA/Tenet 3-4%.

Ortho +8.7% (12% joints, DRG 469/470, da Vinci/Mako 85% facilities). Cardio +6.4% (PCI/TAVR, Medtronic/Edwards). Surgery/neuro +5.1%/+4.8%, OB +1.2%.

Sunbelt: Florida/Texas +7.2%/+6.9% (15% out-of-state patients). Northeast/Midwest +3.1% (United pre-auth delays).

Patient days +4.8% YoY/+1.9% QoQ, trailing due to ALOS 4.62 days (-2% YoY, CMS trends DRG 871/291). APDs +6.1%, CMI 1.72 (+1.8%), ICU days +22%.

Epic MyChart/PINC AI +9% capture, ACO REACH +14% days, Qventus throughput +12%. Medicare days +3.2% (42% 65+), commercial +7.5% (No Surprises).

RN ratio 1:4.8, travelers 18% hours.

Q4 guidance: admissions 4.5-6.0%, days 4.0-5.5%, $250M digital/ortho institutes.

Finally, factors affecting operating margins, which reached 8.2% in Q3, +70 bps YoY from 7.5%—best since pre-pandemic. Revenue +6.5% to $2.1B outpaced expenses +5.2%.

Patient revenue +7.1%, admissions +4.2% to 128K (CV/ortho CMI 1.85 +2.1%), outpatient +9.8% (28 ASCs, 25%+ EBITDA).

Commercial 48% (+4.8% rates), MA +12% (denials 8.2%), Medicaid 14%.

Labor +6.2% to $1.12B (53% revenue), Epic/LeanTaaS cut premium to 4.1% ($28M savings). Supplies +3.9% to $462M (HealthTrust 85% standard, ortho deflation 6.2%, biosimilars), robotics +11% throughput.

Bad debt 2.8%, AWS efficiencies. Sunbelt 9.1% margins vs. Midwest 6.8%.

Target 10%: 35% value-based, AI LOS -0.3 days, telehealth 25%, $450M Texas acquisition +50 bps.

Outpaces peers (6.9% median), offsets IPPS/MA risks via hospital-at-home/ASCs.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Mark to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah outlined so comprehensively, we delivered a solid quarter across volumes, revenues, and margins. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.48 billion, an increase of 8.7% compared to the same period last year. This growth stemmed from higher patient volumes, improved payer dynamics, and effective revenue cycle enhancements.

Our operating expenses were $2.25 billion, representing 90.7% of net revenue, down 50 basis points year-over-year. We maintained tight cost discipline while investing in growth areas like telehealth and ASCs.

Net income for the quarter was $198 million, or $1.56 per diluted share. We are pleased with this performance and confident in hitting our full-year targets.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Laura Bennett for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Laura Bennett:
Thank you, Mark. Good morning. We are advancing meaningfully in clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Comprehensive Heart Care Program has delivered impressive results, including a 25% reduction in 30-day readmission rates. We continue prioritizing technology for better patient experiences and care coordination, notably our expanded telehealth platform, which now handles 20% of follow-ups and has improved access in rural sites.

Following that, Tom Harris will update on operational efficiency.

Tom Harris:
Thank you, Dr. Bennett. We are streamlining operations network-wide for greater efficiency. Key initiatives include our Lean Six Sigma process redesign and centralized supply chain consolidation, yielding $52 million in savings through reduced waste and vendor optimization.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Karen Patel for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Karen Patel:
Thank you, Tom. We remain dedicated to innovation organization-wide. Investments in new technologies and partnerships aim to elevate patient care, boost efficiency, and unlock revenue. Current projects encompass our AI-driven predictive diagnostics platform and blockchain-enabled supply chain tracking, directly tackling care coordination bottlenecks and reducing errors by 15% in pilot phases.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Karen. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of Lean Six Sigma process redesign?

Tom Harris:
Good morning, Jane. Great question. Our Lean Six Sigma initiative, rolled out across 85% of our facilities in Q3, targeted throughput bottlenecks in ED-to-inpatient transitions and OR turnover. By mapping workflows and eliminating non-value-add steps—like redundant documentation—we reduced average ED wait times by 22% and OR case times by 12%, directly translating to $28 million in labor savings from optimized staffing. In our Florida cluster, this freed 150 bed-equivalents daily, accommodating 5% more ortho volumes without added headcount. Complemented by Epic integrations, denial appeals on surgical claims improved 15%, recapturing $8 million. Early FY25 rollout to remaining sites should add another $35 million annualized, supporting margin targets amid labor pressures. Happy to dive deeper offline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Thanks. What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Laura Bennett:
Hi Mike, thanks for the question. Our telehealth platform is a game-changer, now live in all 45 hospitals and scaling to 25% of visits by year-end. In Q3, it drove $45 million in incremental revenue from virtual follow-ups and low-acuity shifts, with 92% patient retention to in-person high-margin procedures. Access improved markedly—rural patient travel reduced 40%, no-show rates down 18%, and chronic care adherence up 22% for CHF/COPD cohorts. Revenue per tele-visit averages $150, but it unlocks $2,500 downstream inpatient equivalents. Guidance embeds 3-4% topline lift in Q4/FY25, offsetting MA scrutiny while enhancing VBC scores. Partnerships like Teladoc bundles position us for CMS innovation payments.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Karen Patel:
Good morning, Sarah. Absolutely. We're allocating $300 million in FY25 capex, 40% to tech/partnerships. Key is our AI diagnostics platform with Google Cloud, piloted in 20 sites, predicting sepsis 24 hours early—cutting LOS 0.5 days and adding $20 million EBITDA. Blockchain supply chain with Vizient traces implants real-time, slashing shortages 30% and negotiating 5% better pricing. Partnerships include Edwards Lifesciences for TAVR site-neutral bundles (15 sites, 20% RPA premium) and Optum for population health analytics on 2M lives. These address coordination gaps, targeting 10% efficiency gains and new streams like $50M precision medicine data licensing. ROI hurdles at 3x payback ensure alignment with 10% margin goal.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Thanks for taking my call. On the margin drivers, how do you see cost controls holding up against potential reimbursement headwinds in 2025?

Mark Reynolds:
Hi David. Solid point. Our 8.2% Q3 margin gives us buffer. Cost controls—LeanTaaS staffing, HealthTrust supplies—should deliver 200 bps expansion, offsetting IPPS -0.4% proposal. Revenue levers like 5% RPA growth and 35% VBC penetration provide insulation. Sunbelt outperformance (9%+ margins) dilutes Northeast drags. If MA denials hit 15%, AI scrubbing mitigates 50%. Dry powder at 3.1x leverage eyes accretive M&A. Confident in 9-10% FY25.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Healthcare Services Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
